text:
Anthony Mantha is on his sixth NHL team, and he has made himself handy in New Jersey. He has 5 goals and 10 points in 17 games in 13:28 a night, none of them on the power play. On Nov. 5 against St. Louis he had two goals and an assist while the Devils finished with 11 forwards and moved him around the lineup, which The Hockey News highlighted as his versatility. Sheldon Keefe, per the Devils' Mike Fink, said he doesn't get enough credit as a passer.

Our numbers say there is more coming. New Jersey takes 57.7 percent of the expected goals at 5v5 with him on the ice, and his team has scored 6.7 fewer goals than those chances deserve. His own finishing is running hot (23.8 percent), so those two may meet in the middle.

He scored 33 goals last season in Pittsburgh. He won't get the same minutes here, but our range still has him around 23 goals. For a depth winger, that is plenty.
headline: Mantha is the Devils' useful man in every slot
